title: Multi-Partner Project: A Model-Driven Engineering Framework for Federated Digital Twins of Industrial Systems (MATISSE)
problem: Federation of multiple digital twins introduces complex challenges in design, development, analysis, deployment, execution and maintenance including identity management, metadata sharing, cross-DT communication/synchronization, and governance that existing single-DT approaches cannot address.
motivation: Digital twins increasingly deployed for monitoring, verification, validation, and testing of complex systems; federation scenarios multiply engineering complexity and necessitate coordinated systems engineering approach.
method: Proposes model-driven engineering framework leveraging traceability as core infrastructural service. Provides conceptual framework for continuous engineering of federated digital twins addressing DT identification, metadata management, cross-DT communication protocols, and federation governance. Demonstrates two concrete industrial scenarios.
key_novelty: Federated digital twin framework with integrated traceability and model-driven continuous engineering for coordination across multiple digital twin systems.
contributions: MATISSE conceptual framework for federated digital twins with emphasis on traceability
Research roadmap for continuous engineering, verification, validation, and monitoring services
Two concrete industrial scenarios demonstrating practical application framework
limitations: Project in initial phase; concrete implementation details, performance metrics, and scalability validation not yet available.
primary_theme: model-driven framework for federated digital twins
